To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the projection of fibers from one area to another is a result of a process which can be understood as a “guided growth” process, where the guiding parameterp is produced within the area of the growth cone and the target tissue.

(1) the growth cones of axons are guided by graded distribution patterns of guiding substances in the nervous system; (2) the generation of these distribution patterns involves graded distributions of components in the projecting and the target area; (3) the components may be activatory or inhibitory in their action on the generation of the guiding substancep; (4) the components may interact directly or indirectly, and may be produced by growth cones and by target tissue; (5) the guiding substancep
the development of neural projections is determined, as a rule, by a combinatorial interaction of graded distributions of factors, in the projecting and in the target area, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a general model for the generation of projections in the central nervous system.
the following questions: What are the mechanisms which generate projections between areas of a nervous system?
the development of projections in the vertebrate nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a projection between two areas of the nervous systems can be described as a result of the interaction and cooperation of components in the growth cone and the target tissue.

the projection of the nervous system can be described as the result of a combinatorial process involving the following components: graded distributions of components in the projecting and the target area, interactions between components, the growth cone and the target, and the interaction of the growth cone with the medium in the target area.

the model is a working hypothesis for a projection mechanism which is based on a few simple assumptions, and is capable of accounting for the major features of projections in the central nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of a projection is a cooperative process, in which the growth cone and the target tissue interact to generate a guiding substance, the distribution of which leads to the formation of the projection.
the formation of projections is the result of the interaction of a large number of components, which are distributed with respect to position, in the projecting and the target area.
a projection is a result of an interaction between the growth cone and the target tissue, which leads to the generation of a guiding parameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a theory of projections can be developed, which is not based on the idea that the nervous system is prepatterned, but which rather emphasizes the role of self-organizing processes in the development of projections.
the projection is not an arbitrary, but rather a highly organized and predictable event in the developing nervous system.
a projection can be generated by a simple interaction of growth cones and target cells in which graded distributions of substances are produced.
